UNDERSTANDING QUANTITY OF HEAT
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what understanding quantity of heat means in plain words.

INTRODUCTION
----
Understanding Quantity of Heat. Get clear on quantity of heat before moving on. How would you explain quantity of heat to a classmate in one minute? Use this anchor: Explain the terminologies used quantity of heat,. Clue from the topic: Heat and specific latent heat. Check every example on this page against that anchor.

MAIN NOTES
----
• Quantity of heat (Q) measures thermal energy transferred because of a temperature difference or a change of state.
• Temperature change (no change of state): Q = mcΔθ.
• Heat capacity of an object: C = Q/Δθ = mc.
• Change of state at constant temperature: Q = mL.
• Never confuse heat (energy in joules) with temperature (°C or K). Heat can flow while temperature stays constant during a change of state.
• Show method: identify process → pick formula → substitute with units → compute → check whether the answer size is sensible.

SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

• Say what specific heat capacity means in plain words.
• Give one clear example linked to Quantity of Heat.

INTRODUCTION
----
Specific heat capacity. Focus on specific heat capacity. Take one clear example of specific heat capacity. Watch this detail: Heat and specific latent heat. Underneath it sits this rule: Determine the specific heat capacity of various substances,. Name it correctly, then apply it.

MAIN NOTES
----
• Specific heat capacity (c) is the heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K (or 1 °C).
• Formula: Q = mcΔθ (also written Q = mcΔT), where Δθ is the temperature change.
• Heat capacity (C) of a body is the heat needed to raise that whole body’s temperature by 1 K: C = mc = Q/Δθ.
• Different materials store heat differently — water has a high specific heat capacity, so it heats and cools slowly.
• In calorimetry, heat lost by a hot body equals heat gained by a cold body and calorimeter (if no heat escapes).
• Always convert mass to kg (or keep g consistently) and use °C or K differences the same way (Δθ size is identical).

LATENT HEAT
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what latent heat means in plain words.
• Give one clear example linked to Quantity of Heat.
• Correct one common mistake about this page.

INTRODUCTION
----
Latent heat. Focus on latent heat. Learners often mix up latent heat with a nearby idea. Keep this accurate line instead: Demonstrate factors affecting boiling points and melting points of different substances,. Supporting detail: Heat and specific latent heat.

MAIN NOTES
----
• Latent heat is the heat energy absorbed or released during a change of state at constant temperature.
• Quantity of heat for a change of state: Q = mL, where m is mass and L is specific latent heat.
• Specific latent heat of fusion (L_f) is heat to change 1 kg solid ↔ liquid at melting point without temperature change.
• Specific latent heat of vaporisation (L_v) is heat to change 1 kg liquid ↔ vapour at boiling point without temperature change.
• During melting or boiling the thermometer reading stays steady while heat is still being supplied — that heat is latent heat.
• Units: Q in joules (J), m in kg, L in J/kg (or J/g if mass is in grams — keep units consistent).

WORKED EXAMPLE
----
Worked example — specific latent heat of fusion:
Find the heat needed to change 0.2 kg of ice at 0 °C to water (no temperature change).

Working:
1. Formula / relationship: Q = mL
2. Substitute values: Q = 0.2 × 334000
3. Q = 66800
Final Answer: 66800 J
Mark reminder: method mark for Q = mL; accuracy mark with joules
Wrong path: using Q = mcΔθ here — temperature is constant during the change of state, so latent heat applies.
